settings.question: How do I build and launch a production-ready website with Claude Code?
settings.body: Planning, platform build systems for Shopify, WordPress, Astro, SaaS and landing pages, a production CLAUDE.md, security and accessibility audits, 100 reusable prompts and the launch checklists. It is the system for getting from nothing to live without shipping the mistakes that are cheap now and expensive later.

settings.question: My website exists. Why is nobody finding it?
settings.body: Twenty audit prompts in dependency order: crawlability first, then canonicals, then indexing decisions, then metadata, then speed. Each one demands evidence rather than a summary, and none of them is allowed to fix anything in the same run.
settings.cta_label: See the SEO & Website Audit Toolkit

settings.question: People arrive and nothing happens. Where am I losing them?
settings.body: Thirteen modules and 70 workflows for finding where a site loses conversions, ranking what to fix, and proving the fix worked. Every finding carries evidence and an honesty label, and the experimentation system tells you when you do not have the traffic to test at all.

settings.question: It is live, found and converting. How do I keep it that way?
settings.body: Seventeen modules, 19 slash commands and 11 standard-library scripts for the stage that lasts longest: daily health checks with a score, weekly security and link checks, tested backups, dependency updates in batches with rollback points, a gate on both sides of every deploy, incident playbooks and a monthly report. Every change follows seven phases and none touches production without your yes.

settings.question: I own the whole lifecycle, and I will meet the first three of these.
settings.body: The three systems together, delivered as three downloads on one order. Nothing in it is exclusive to the bundle and nothing is abridged — it is the same three products at the same versions, for less than buying them separately. Both figures are shown on its page.
settings.cta_label: See the Complete Site Builder Stack

settings.question: My store runs on Shopify and the catalogue is too big to manage by hand. What now?
settings.body: Nineteen modules, 34 slash commands, 32 standard-library scripts and 18 validated GraphQL documents for the Shopify admin: export and audit the catalogue, fix products, collections, SEO, metafields, alt text and redirects from reviewed files, run bulk operations on any catalogue size — every write previewed against the live value, backed up and read back. A specialist toolkit for one platform; the four stages before it apply to any site.

settings.question: The site has to move — new platform, new host, new domain, new URLs. How do I not lose what it has?
settings.body: Twenty modules including seven platform guides, 37 slash commands and 28 standard-library scripts for the weeks a site is moving: every URL inventoried and mapped, redirects generated for six platforms and tested on the real origin, metadata and structured data compared page by page, DNS recorded before it is touched, staging validated, a cutover that quotes each change, a rollback that is a procedure, and a scorecard that says GO, GO WITH WARNINGS or NO-GO. Applies to any platform pair; the guides carry the platform facts.

settings.question: I do this for clients. How do I run the engagement as well as I build the site?
settings.body: Twenty-one modules, 37 slash commands, 29 templates, 17 checklists and one complete fictional engagement for the work around the work: qualifying, discovering, auditing with evidence, scoping with counts, estimating as a range, proposing, onboarding, planning, delivering against a definition of done, reviewing in bounded rounds, launching on evidence, handing off in plain language, reporting with sourced numbers, and turning the finished project into a retainer built from what the site needs. Not a stage of the website; the operating system of the business that builds them.
settings.cta_label: See the Agency & Client Delivery System

settings.heading: Build, then rank, then convert, then operate — migrate when you must, and deliver it for clients
settings.intro: Each stage has its own product because each needs different evidence, different workflows and a different definition of done. The fourth is the one you will use every week for as long as the site exists; the fifth is for the weeks it moves; the sixth is for Shopify stores only; the seventh is for people who do all of this for clients.
settings.note: Buying one product does not include the others and there is no upgrade credit — someone who owns one product and later wants the bundle would be paying for that product twice. Worth knowing before you choose.
